## Purpose

The St Helena Diabetes Registry is a REDCap-based system for improving the organisation of diabetes care and producing decision-ready population reporting.  It is designed to account for the current healthcare reality in St Helena, in which clinical information remains fragmented across legacy software, spreadsheets and paper-based workarounds, while a new Electronic Medical Record (EMR) system is being implemented.

The registry is not intended to replace a whole EMR.  In its first release it records information collected or reviewed by the diabetes team, supports structured recall and follow-up, and provides an auditable source for a pre-defined group of internationally recognised diabetes metrics.  It is designed so that its data can later be linked to, or migrated into, a more mature Health Information System environment.

## Care model and patient journey

The first operational pathway records information gathered at two linked patient contacts.  Blood-taking visits start on **1 September 2026**.  Follow-up consultation visits begin around **mid-September 2026**, on receipt of and after review of blood results.  At the consultation, the diabetes team conduct a holistic review with the patient. 

The registry supports a planned six-monthly diabetes-team review rhythm, while allowing separate event records for blood tests, medicine changes, foot and eye care, and lifestyle interventions.

## Registry database design principles

- `internal_redcap_id` is the internal registry key; `sh_diabetes_id` is the public registry patient identifier (which still needs to be developed).
- EMIS and PatientSource identifiers are retained as separate linkage fields.  ASET identifiers are specimen/request-level identifiers, not patient identifiers.
- Repeating Table 2 is a restricted contact, residence, vital-status and follow-up history form. It preserves changing addresses and contact details, migration episodes, vital status and follow-up outcomes; clinical and analytical users should not need routine access to identifiers.
- Only accepted laboratory results are used in routine reporting.
- The initial data collection focuses on the core field set. Extended fields are deferred or hidden unless a clear clinical workflow requires them.
- All reporting definitions, exclusions, time windows and missing-data handling are specified in the Statistical Analysis Plan.

Database table details are presented below:

| Table | Instrument | Record pattern | Primary role | Key variables / groups |
|--|---|---:|---|----|
| 1 | Baseline | Single | Registry identifiers and demographic variables | `internal_redcap_id`<br>`sh_diabetes_id`<br>EMIS and PatientSource IDs<br>Date of registry entry<br>Date of birth<br>Sex |
| 2 | Contact, residence, vital status and follow-up history | Repeating, restricted | Maintains changing contact and address details, residence/migration, vital status, review due dates and default/re-engagement history | Names and previous name<br>Telephone numbers and email<br>Address episode and usual residence<br>Migration/overseas-care status<br>Vital status and date of death<br>Follow-up status, missed-review count and reason |
| 3 | Diagnosis and confirmation | Single | Diabetes classification, type and date of diagnosis | Registry classification<br>Diabetes type<br>Diagnosis date/year<br>Age at diagnosis<br>Diagnosis confirmation status<br>Diagnosis review date |
| 4 | Physical review | Repeating | Blood pressure, height, weight and BMI | Measurement date<br>Systolic and diastolic BP readings<br>Final analytic BP<br>Height<br>Weight<br>BMI and BMI category |
| 5 | Laboratory results | Repeating | Accepted diabetes-team reviewed laboratory result bundles | Specimen date<br>ASET/request identifier<br>Result acceptance status<br>HbA1c and method status<br>Renal function and urine ACR<br>Lipid results<br>Other safety blood results |
| 6 | Lifestyle and preventive care | Repeating | Education, dietary review, vaccination, pregnancy advice and interventions | Intervention/review date<br>Intervention type and status<br>Provider role<br>Structured education<br>Dietary review<br>Influenza immunisation<br>Pregnancy/pre-conception advice<br>Smoking status |
| 7 | Foot review | Repeating | Foot assessment, risk and referral | Foot examination date<br>Completion and overall result<br>Foot-risk category<br>Current ulcer<br>Podiatry referral<br>Detailed circulation/sensation findings |
| 8 | Eye review and referral | Repeating | Eye screening, result, referral and due date | Eye examination date<br>Completion status<br>Retinopathy result<br>Eye referral date and status<br>Next due date<br>Maculopathy result |
| 9 | Medication review | Repeating | Current treatment and medication review | Medication-review date and completion<br>Medication date and status<br>Medication type and class<br>Diabetes-medication category<br>Antihypertensive and ACE-I/ARB flags<br>Detailed prescribing information |

## Reporting framework

The registry will report the full M01--M26 metric set. M01--M19 describe burden, clinical control and care quality; M20 monitors diagnosis confirmation; and M21--M26 monitor delivery of the structured diabetes-care pathway. The associated Statistical Analysis Plan is the authoritative source for metric definitions.

## Follow-up, default and migration status

Vital status remains deliberately simple: **alive**, **deceased** or **unknown**. It is distinct from attendance and migration. Table 2 records the longitudinal status needed for safe recall and denominator management.

For the initial six-monthly care pathway, a person is **potentially defaulted** when one scheduled diabetes-team review is missed and remains incomplete after a 30-day grace period. A person is **definitely defaulted** when two consecutive scheduled six-monthly reviews are missed (normally at least 12 months since the last completed review), following at least one documented attempt to contact or trace them. A later completed review records **re-engaged** status while preserving the earlier history.

Temporary overseas employment, overseas medical care, transfer to another provider, permanent migration and other documented reasons are recorded separately as the reason for missed or ceased local follow-up. They should not be misclassified as unknown default.

## Governance and implementation boundary

The registry starts as a diabetes-team system. It does not retrospectively treat free-text entries in existing clinical systems as a fully reliable automated feed. Legacy data can support case ascertainment and clinical review, but new registry data should be entered, reviewed and audited under defined rules.

**Before go-live, the registry team must agree the diagnosis-confirmation rule, active-resident denominator rule, default/re-engagement and migration rules, data-access roles, laboratory identity and acceptance procedure, and first reporting date.**
